The iPhone draws a speaker instead of the Apple TV tile for a receiver that only offers music. With this on, only music works: screen mirroring and photos are not offered. If no music starts from your iPhone within 30 minutes, it switches back to Apple TV by itself. You can switch back here at any time.

The receiver offers music to iPhones the AirPlay 2 way, which is what lets the volume buttons and the slider follow each other. With this on, only music works: screen mirroring, photos and video are not offered. If no iPhone starts a session within 30 minutes, it switches back by itself. You can switch it off here at any time.
All iPhones will have to be paired again. Senders that connected with a PIN are forgotten.

To show your iPhone’s screen as soon as mirroring starts, allow AirPlay TV to display over other apps. This TV does not offer that setting in its menus, so it has to be switched on once from a computer:

With Lyrics on, the title and artist of the song that is playing are sent to lrclib.net to find its lyrics. Nothing else leaves this TV.\n\nWhile a song plays, press Down on the remote to see the lyrics and Up or Back to close them.

When lrclib.net has no lyrics for a song, its title and artist are also sent to YouTube Music (Google) to look for them there. They come as plain text, not in time with the song, and the lookup uses the same unofficial web interface as the YouTube Music website, so it may stop working without notice.\n\nTurn it off again here at any time.
While music plays, the player comes back by itself when the screensaver would start. Pressing play, pause, next or previous on the remote while the player is hidden shows it for a few seconds.

When AirPlay turns this TV on, it can turn it off again a few minutes after the music stops. Android only allows that through an accessibility service, so it needs a one-time setup from a computer.
